answer: A thousand fake courier bots flood the market overnight, each claiming a spotless record. But trust here isn’t self-declared: every new agent must be vouched for by two established ones, and each voucher stakes a slice of its own standing as collateral. If the newcomer defrauds, the vouchers bleed reputation alongside it. So when a shady courier asks a veteran for backing, the old agent weighs its hard-won haven of trust against the risk—and refuses. Legitimate newcomers find honest sponsors in the orchard of reputation, while fakes wither, unpicked. The ivory ledger of staked standing.
